Estimate a block jackknife standard error from per locus estimates

Source: R/jackknife_stats_generic.R
jackknife_stats_generic.Rd

This function is mostly designed for developers: it is a general function to estimate the genome-wide value of a statistic, together with its standard error, using a weighted block jackknife. It takes a vector of per locus estimates, and aggregates them by sum or mean (or a custom function), leaving out one block of loci at a time. To compute specific quantities directly from a gen_tibble, use the appropriate jackknife_* functions, e.g jackknife_pairwise_pop_fst() to compute pairwise Fst.

Usage

jackknife_stats_generic(
  .x,
  loci_table,
  operator = c("mean", "sum", "custom"),
  block_size,
  size_unit = c("snp", "cM", "bp"),
  f = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

.x

A vector containing the per locus estimates.

loci_table

a dataframe including at least a column 'chromosome', and additionally a column 'position' if size_unit is "bp", or a column 'genetic_dist' if size_unit is "cM".

operator

The operator to use to aggregate the per locus estimates. Either "mean", "sum" or "custom" to use a custom function f.

block_size

The size of the blocks to leave out.

size_unit

Either "snp", "cM" or "bp". If "snp", the block size is in number of SNPs. If "cM", the block size is in centiMorgans. If "bp", the block size is in base pairs.

f

a custom function to use for the statistic. This function should take a vector of locus estimates and return a single value. Note that, for a custom function, the statistic is recomputed from scratch for every block, which is slower than using "mean" or "sum".

...

Additional arguments to be passed to the custom operator function.

Value

A tibble with columns: 'estimate' (the statistic computed on all loci), 'jack_estimate' (the bias corrected jackknife estimate), 'se' (the jackknife standard error), 'z' (the z score, jack_estimate/se), and 'n_blocks' (the number of blocks used).

Details

The genome is divided into non-overlapping blocks, which never span more than one chromosome. Blocks can be defined as a number of SNPs, a number of base pairs, or a size in centiMorgans (which requires the 'genetic_dist' column of the loci table to be filled in). The statistic is then recomputed leaving out one block at a time, and the standard error is computed with the weighted delete-m jackknife of Busing et al. (1999), where each block is weighted by the number of loci with non-missing values that it contains. Blocks should be larger than the extent of linkage disequilibrium (e.g. 5 cM, or a few Mb).

References

Busing FMTA, Meijer E, Van Der Leeden R (1999) Delete-m jackknife for unequal m. Statistics and Computing 9:3-8.

Examples

example_gt <- load_example_gt("gen_tbl")

miss_by_locus <- loci_missingness(example_gt)

# Calculate the mean missingness and its standard error,
# using blocks of 2 SNPs
jackknife_stats_generic(miss_by_locus,
  loci_table = show_loci(example_gt),
  operator = "mean", block_size = 2,
  size_unit = "snp"
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   estimate jack_estimate     se     z n_blocks
#>      <dbl>         <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>    <int>
#> 1   0.0952        0.0952 0.0238     4        3
